title_or_hook: College prospect threshold filters: WR four-bar filter + QB under-pressure profile (2 posts)
summary: Two "only players who clear every bar" filters over college charting data, both tables browser-transcribed from the opened feed posts. (a) WR filter, FBS prospects since 2018, best college season: over 75% of routes out wide, aDOT over 12.5, contested catch rate over 50%, contested target rate vs zone under 7.5%. Five names clear it (CTT% / CTC% / aDOT / wide%): KJ Duff (Rutgers) 7.41 / 61.1 / 15.6 / 94.1, Romeo Doubs 6.15 / 60.0 / 13.8 / 89.3, Chris Olave 5.88 / 62.5 / 18.8 / 89.1, Denzel Boston 6.25 / 76.9 / 14.4 / 81.3, Charlie Becker 6.82 / 76.5 / 15.6 / 76.5. (b) QB filter, P4 round-1 draftees since 2012, best college season: big-time throw rate under pressure under 5.0%, turnover-worthy play rate under pressure over 5.0%, pressure-to-sack rate under 11.11%. Two names clear it: Ryan Tannehill (3.9 / 5.7 / 5.9) and Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State (4.8 / 8.6 / 10.8). The QB post's own framing is honest: subpar under-pressure production with one historical precedent is a warning shape, not an endorsement. All values CITED from the post's tables, UNVERIFIED. The transferable asset is the filter shape, not the names. Risks: "best season" selection is survivorship by construction; thresholds look tuned to produce a short list (11.11% is a suspiciously exact bar); contested-catch charting is human-coded and not in nflverse; college-to-NFL transfer is unproven for both filters. Denzel Boston also appears in W7's rookie scrimmage-yards list - cross-post corroboration inside one run.

QB under-pressure profile: BTT rate under 5.0%, TWP rate over 5.0%, pressure-to-sack rate under 11.11% (P4 round-1 draftees since 2012)
